source_discovered: Luminosity and Physics Considerations on HL-LHC and HE-LHC based µp Colliders
version: arXiv:1905.05564v2 (read); EPL 138 (2022) 24002 per the earlier search record — peer reviewed; journal version not seen
relevance: Earlier LHC-based μp collider proposal of the AloHEP group (precursor of μLHC, SRC_ARXIV_2506_15445): a muon collider tangential to the HL-LHC or HE-LHC (Fig. 1). Inputs: Table 1 HL-LHC/HE-LHC (√s 14/27 TeV, N_p 2.2e11, 2760/2808 bunches, σ_z 90 mm, ε_N 2.5 µm, β* 0.15/0.45 m, σ 7.1/9 µm, 5e34/16e34); Table 2 ERL60-upgraded protons (N_p 2.2/2.5e11, ε_N 2/2.5 µm, β* 7/10 cm, σ 4.45/4.17 µm); Table 3 muon collider [Delahaye et al., arXiv:1901.06150] (√s 1.5/3/6 TeV, 2.5/4.5/6 km, N_μ 2e12, σ_z 1/0.5/0.2 cm, ε_N 25 µm, β* 1/0.5/0.25 cm, σ 5.9/2.95/1.48 µm, 15/12/6 Hz, 2 IPs, L_μμ 1.25/4.4/12e34). Eq. (6) L_μp = (N_p/N_μ)(σ_μ/max[σ_p,σ_μ])² L_μμ gives Table 4 (HL-LHC: √s 4.58/6.48/9.16 TeV for E_μ 0.75/1.5/3 TeV; L 0.95/0.84/0.57e33 nominal, 1.4/2.1/1.5e33 upgraded) and Table 5 (HE-LHC: √s 6.36/9/12.7 TeV; 0.59/0.52/0.36e33 and 1.6/2.8/1.9e33). Table 6 matched-beam tune shifts (eqs. 9-10): ξ_p 0.098/0.12/0.098/0.098, ξ_μ 0.0096/0.0096/0.0096/0.011, with the statement (p. 5) that 'ξp values should be reduced by an order … resulting in corresponding decrease of luminosity'. Table 7 x_min at Q² = 1 and 25 GeV². All 12 luminosities and 8 tune shifts reproduce from the printed equations (tests/scientific/test_batch10_documents.py).
unresolved_questions: Eq. (6) rescales the muon collider's average luminosity L_μμ, so the μ+μ− two-beam decay average (and the muon-collider repetition rate and hourglass factor) are carried into μp, where only the muon beam decays (cf. tests/scientific/test_batch7_documents.py::test_decay_averaging_differs_between_mumu_and_mup); the paper does not discuss this — CONF_LUMI_MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS. | No hourglass factor for μp although the proton rms bunch length (90 mm, Table 1) is 9-36 times the muon β* (0.25-1 cm, Table 3); quantifying it needs a beam-beam/luminosity code run, not done here. | Eq. (1) uses 4π max[σ_xp,σ_xμ] max[σ_yp,σ_yμ] instead of the Gaussian overlap 2π√(σ_xp²+σ_xμ²)√(σ_yp²+σ_yμ²): identical for matched beams, conservative by up to a factor 2 for very unequal sizes; the tables therefore equal the matched-beam luminosity, which is also the configuration of Table 6 (eqs. 9-10). | Collision frequency min[f_cp, f_cμ] assumes every muon passage meets a proton bunch; synchronisation of the two rings and the LHC abort gap (2760 of 3564 slots filled) are not discussed. | By the paper's own statement (p. 5) ξ_p is an order of magnitude too high; for matched beams L ∝ ξ_p at fixed N_p, γ_p, β*_p, so either named remedy (N_μ ÷ 10 or ε_N,p × 10) lowers every Table 4-5 value tenfold, i.e. to 0.04-0.28e33 — this beam-beam-compatible order is not stated in the abstract ('of order of 1e33'). | Printed radii r_p = 1.54e-18 m and r_μ = 1.37e-17 m are 0.3 % and 0.5 % above r_e m_e/m (1.535e-18, 1.363e-17 m); immaterial for Table 6. | Journal version (EPL 138 (2022) 24002) not seen; only the arXiv v2 file was read.

source_discovered: Enhancement of muonium emission rate from silica aerogel with a laser ablated surface
version: arXiv 1407.8248v1 [physics.ins-det] 31 Jul 2014 (read); PTEP 2014 (9) 091C01 as cited by SRC_DOI_10_7566_JPSCP_33_011125 ref. [8]; journal version not seen
relevance: Laser-ablated silica-aerogel muonium emitter — the target technology of the J-PARC g-2/EDM ultra-slow-muon source and of μTRISTAN. Fabrication (p. 3): femtosecond laser 800 nm, 230 fs, 0.6 mJ/pulse, 1 kHz, 30 µm spot, 800 pulses (0.8 s) per hole; 29 mg cm^-3, 7 mm aerogel; 270 µm holes 4.5-5.0 mm deep on a 300/400/500 µm triangular pitch over 30 × 30 mm²; measured mass loss only 5-10 % of that expected from the hole geometry. Measurement (pp. 4-5): TRIUMF M15 subsurface muons, ~1e4 s^-1, ~23.0 MeV/c, Δp/p 5 % FWHM, ~50 % stopping, 8 mT vertical field, ~2 mm RMS vertex resolution. Table 1, Mu yield in vacuum regions 1-3 (10-40 mm) per 1e3 muon stops: flat 3.72 ± 0.11; flat (Bakule 2013, SRC_ARXIV_1306_3810) 2.74 ± 0.11; ablated pitch 500/400/300 µm 16.0 ± 0.2 / 20.9 ± 0.7 / 30.5 ± 0.3 (statistical; systematic ≈ 4 % ablated, ≈ 1 % flat) — 30.5/3.72 = 8.2, 'at least eight times'; the 300 µm yield is 3 % of muons decaying in target + vacuum. J-PARC projection (pp. 5-6): 28 MeV/c, 5 % RMS; 0.01 Mu per incident muon (near-surface assumption of Bakule 2013); ultra-slow muon rate 0.2e6 s^-1, 'five times smaller than the design intensity' (1e6 s^-1, p. 2); 0.4 ppm g-2 in 1e7 s at 50 % polarisation. Gives NO muonium formation fraction.
unresolved_questions: The 0.52 formation fraction, the fitted T = 322 K / D = 870 cm² s^-1 and the 23.2 mg cm^-3, 8.8 mm sample that Zhang et al. 2021 (SRC_DOI_10_7566_JPSCP_33_011125, ref. [8]) attribute to this paper are not in it (samples here are 29 mg cm^-3, 7 mm) — CONF_MUONIUM_FORMATION_FRACTION provenance trail. | Table 1 yields are for decays 10-40 mm from the surface, not total emission; converting to a total emission probability needs the diffusion/velocity model (Bakule 2013 gives 0.3 % → 1.0 % for flat aerogel). | The 0.4 ppm projection (p. 6) cannot be re-derived from the printed numbers alone (running time and polarisation assumed for the 0.1 ppm design are not printed). | Journal version (PTEP 2014, 091C01) not seen; only the arXiv v1 was read.

source_discovered: Simulation Study of Laser Ionization of Muonium by 1S-2S Excitation for the Muon g - 2/EDM Experiment at J-PARC
version: JPS Conf. Proc. 33, 011125 (2021); Proc. 3rd J-PARC Symposium (J-PARC2019); received 10 Jan 2020
relevance: Simulated yield chain of the J-PARC MLF S-line (S2) demonstration of muonium laser ionisation by 1S-2S two-photon excitation (244 nm) plus 355 nm ionisation — the 244 nm alternative to the 122 nm Lyman-α scheme. Table I (p. 6): S-line transport to S2 0.00717 → 2.4e6 s^-1; surface-muon stopping 0.467 → 1.1e6; Mu formation 0.52 → 5.8e5; Mu vacuum yield 0.082 → 4.8e4; laser ionisation 3.9e-7 → 0.0186; slow-beamline transmission 0.651 → 0.0121; MCP 0.90 → 0.0109 s^-1 ('about 0.011/s'). Inputs: G4Beamline S-line model validated on S1 (1.9e5, 500 kW); 100 µm Kapton window, 435 µm Al degrader, 78 × 78 × 6 mm aerogel, mean stopping time ~350 ns (p. 3); 3-D random-walk diffusion with T = 322 K, D = 870 cm² s^-1 (p. 3-4); laser region 2 × 40 × 2 mm³ centred 3 mm from the surface, optimum delay 0.8 µs (p. 4); 1S→2S probability 8.8e-7 × 2S→ionisation ~44 % = 3.9e-7 per vacuum Mu including spatial and temporal overlap, 'preliminary', optical Bloch equations (p. 4); SOA lens 20 kV, ED 5 kV, muSRsim extraction (p. 5-6). Earliest archived 244 nm ionisation estimate: 3.9e-7 vs ~1e-6 (Zhang 2026 Kraków deck, 1.5 mJ) and 7e-6-6e-5 (Aritome et al. 2024, 0.5-1.3 mJ) — CONF_LASER_IONISATION_EFFICIENCY.
unresolved_questions: S2 surface-muon intensity: '2.4 × 10^5/s per pulse at 500 kW' (§2, p. 3) vs '2.4×10^6 per pulse at 500 kW' (§5, p. 6) and 2.4×10^6 s^-1 (Table I): a factor 10 inside the paper; the final 0.011 s^-1 uses 2.4e6. | Stopping efficiency 44.3 % (p. 3, 435 µm degrader) vs 0.467 in Table I (p. 6). | Extraction: 1.5e3 of 2.0e3 generated thermal muons reach the MCP (0.75), while the transmission is stated as (58.6 ± 0.9) % 'including 13% of decay-loss, 85% of the mesh transmission efficiency and the 90% of MCP aperture ratio' (p. 6); the three named factors multiply to 0.666; Table I splits 0.586 as 0.651 × 0.90. How 0.75, 0.586 and 0.666 relate is not explained. | The 52 % formation fraction, T = 322 K, D = 870 cm² s^-1 and the best sample (23.2 mg cm^-3, 8.8 mm) are all cited to Beer et al. 2014 [8] (SRC_ARXIV_1407_8248), which contains none of them: 0.52 ± 0.01 is Bakule et al. 2013 p. 3 (MuSR, SRC_ARXIV_1306_3810); the sample matches Beare et al. 2020 p. 5 (23.2-23.6 mg cm^-3, 8.7-8.9 mm, SRC_ARXIV_2006_01947); T and D appear in the Zhang 2026 Kraków deck p. 7 ('fitted against the data collected at TRIUMF', SRC_WS1681458_ZHANG_MUONIUM). The primary publication of the T/D fit is not identified. | Whether the simulated aerogel is laser-ablated is not stated; laser pulse energies of the 244 nm/355 nm system are not printed (excitation simulation from ref. [9], private communication).

source_discovered: Feasibility demonstration of a high-momentum, high-purity muon beamline at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility
relevance: J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility B-line 'µ20' mode: tertiary muons from backward π decay in a ~7 m drift (v23-h24), downstream optics scaled to 60-85 % of the upstream momentum; p_μ ≈ (m_μ²/m_π²) p_π ≈ 0.57 p_π (p. 6). T106 measurements at 3/5/10 GeV/c upstream: Table 1 hadrons 0.2/0.6/1.4 M/spill (π:p 0.66:0.34, 0.60:0.40, 0.39:0.61); Table 2 muons 0.42-17.0 k/spill; Table 3 purities 53.2-98.3 %; headline 1.7e3 µ/spill at 3 GeV/c (5 GeV/c × 60 %) with purity 98.0 ± 0.6 % (97.9 ± 0.9 % with the empirical 3 GeV/c hadron template) and σ ≈ 15 mm (pp. 1, 11, 16-19). 30 GeV slow extraction, 2 s spill per 4.24 s cycle; secondaries from the beam loss (several hundred W) at a Lambertson septum; a planned 15 kW-loss target should raise the µ20 rate by more than two orders of magnitude (>1e5/spill, p. 17). Context only for LHμC: a conventional GeV/c tertiary muon beam for radiography; it backs no LHμC parameter.
unresolved_questions: p. 10: 85 % 'corresponds to the laboratory momentum of muons emitted at 90° in the center-of-mass frame'; relativistic two-body kinematics give p_μ/p_π = (1 + m_μ²/m_π²)/2 = 0.787 at 90° (tests/scientific/test_batch10_documents.py). The stated 85 % upper limit is therefore not the 90° point; this does not affect the measured values. | Unrefereed arXiv v1 (26 Aug 2026); the T106 proposal (KEK/J-PARC-PAC 2025-39) behind the ±5 % momentum-bite simulation was not read.
